title: Adoption
definition: Adoption is God’s gracious act of receiving believers as His children through Jesus Christ.
summary: Adoption is God’s gracious act of receiving believers as His children through Jesus Christ.
christFocus: Jesus, the eternal Son, brings believers into the Father’s family so they may know God as Father by the Spirit of adoption.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Adoption means salvation includes belonging. God does not only pardon sinners as a judge; He receives them as a Father. In Christ, believers are brought into the family of God.

This adoption is not earned by background, usefulness, strength, or social acceptance. It is granted by grace through union with Christ. Believers receive a new identity, inheritance, access, and family relationship with God.

The Holy Spirit bears witness that believers are children of God and teaches them to cry, “Abba, Father.” Adoption shows the tenderness of salvation: God brings His people near, not merely out of danger but into His household.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people feel unwanted, rejected, abandoned, or unusable. Adoption speaks the heart of Christ into that wound: those who belong to Him are not spiritual orphans but beloved children of the Father.

This doctrine also reshapes obedience. Children of God do not obey to earn a place at the table; they obey because grace has brought them home.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Live as a child of God in Christ. Bring your fear of rejection to the Father, rely on the Spirit’s witness, and treat other believers as family members Christ has welcomed by grace.
